summary: The note introduces the geographic position of Myanmar (also known as Burma) as the northwesternmost country of mainland Southeast Asia. It lists the countries it borders, describes its location relative to the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates and the Himalayas, names the seas to its west and south, and notes its strategic position near major Indian Ocean shipping lanes.
one_line: Overview of Myanmar's location in mainland Southeast Asia, its bordering countries, tectonic setting, surrounding seas, and strategic shipping position.
key_facts: Myanmar, also known as Burma, is the northwestern-most country of mainland Southeast Asia.
Myanmar borders China, India, Bangladesh, Thailand and Laos.
Myanmar lies along the Indian and Eurasian Plates.
Myanmar lies to the southeast of the Himalayas.
The Bay of Bengal is to the west of Myanmar.
The Andaman Sea is to the south of Myanmar.
Myanmar is strategically located near major Indian Ocean shipping lanes.
